name: AI Job Search
cost: Free (MIT). Claude Code has no free tier, so you need a Claude Pro, Max or Team plan or Anthropic API credits
works_with: Claude Code. The portal search skills also work in Codex, Antigravity and Gemini CLI through `AGENTS.md`
short: A job search kit for Claude Code that scores postings against your profile, tailors your CV and cover letter, and preps you for interviews.
what: You copy the repo, fill in your profile, and run slash commands in Claude Code. `/scrape` searches job portals and sorts matches by fit. `/apply` scores a posting, drafts a LaTeX CV and cover letter, has a second agent review them, then compiles and checks the PDFs. More commands handle interview prep, follow-ups and a tracker dashboard.
who: Job seekers who are happy working in a terminal and want tailored applications without writing each one from scratch. The bundled portal searches are mostly Danish, so outside Denmark you'll lean on the LinkedIn and freehire searches or build your own with `/add-portal`. If you don't want to install LaTeX or pay for Claude Code, skip it.
needs: Claude Code with a paid Claude plan or Anthropic API credits
Bun, for the job search tools
A LaTeX install with `lualatex` and `xelatex`, such as TeX Live, MacTeX, TinyTeX or MiKTeX
Optional: `pip install pypdf` for the CV's ATS check

steps.title: Get your own copy
steps.text: Forks of this repo are always public. For your own job search, the README says to make a private repo with this one as `upstream` instead (SETUP.md section 8 shows how). Fork only if you plan to contribute.

steps.title: Install the job search tools
steps.text: Run this inside the repo folder. On Windows use `python tools\install_portal_clis.py`. Add `--dry-run` to see what it would install first.

steps.title: Set up your profile
steps.text: Start Claude Code with `claude`, then run this. It reads your `documents/` folder, takes a CV pasted into the chat, or interviews you.

steps.title: Search for jobs
steps.text: Use `/rank` afterwards if you get more results than you want to read.

steps.title: Apply to a job
steps.text: If the site blocks the fetch, paste the full job description after `/apply` instead.

try.label: From the README
try.text: After `/setup`, run `/scrape`, pick a match, then run `/apply` on it to get a tailored CV and cover letter.

watch: `/setup` writes your name, contact details, work history and salary expectations into tracked files. A fork is always public, so use a private repo.
Job postings come in from outside. The workflow is told to ignore instructions in them, but the README says this is not a sandbox, so check what was written before you send anything.
The `linkedin-search` tool uses LinkedIn's public job endpoints. The README says automated access breaks LinkedIn's terms, so it's for personal use at low volume.
Portal tools you copy from other people's forks run pre-approved on your machine. The README says to read all their code first.
`/gmail-sync` reads your Gmail through a connector and `/notion-sync` writes to Notion. Both are optional, and `/gmail-sync` asks before it writes anything.
The README says the project has no crypto token or paid sponsorship. Treat any such claim as a scam.
